context.why:
US-1 landed the component and the package's own Plans page inside the Account Center; US-2 wired the signed-in person's address onto the element. Both of those are about a page this package ships and routes.

This story is about the other place plans go: somebody else's template. A project building on this package wants plans on its public landing page too, and the Account Center cannot serve that page — a landing page has no signed-in person, no view of ours, and no reason to involve our routing at all.

The claim being tested is that the component is genuinely self-sufficient. Given a pricing table identifier and a publishable key as attributes, it must produce the complete element with no view, no context processor, and no query against the backend, for a reader who is not signed in. If that claim already holds, T016 passes the moment it is written, and that is a real result rather than a problem — the design intended it. SAY SO PLAINLY IN YOUR REPORT: state whether T016 was red before T018 or passed on first run. Do not manufacture a failure to make the cycle look conventional, and do not weaken the test so that it fails.

T018 is the demonstration of the same thing: the component placed on the demo's landing page, the page a visitor reaches without signing in, with a line of copy saying this is the same component the Account Center's Plans page renders.

The demonstration project is already serving this branch on port 8020 with autoreload, so a broken template is visible immediately at http://127.0.0.1:8020/ — you do not need to start it and must not restart it.

THE PROVIDER'S ELEMENT — The provider is Stripe and the element is <stripe-pricing-table>. Its attributes: 'pricing-table-id' (required), 'publishable-key' (required), 'customer-email' (optional, wired in US-2). The element is brought to life by https://js.stripe.com/v3/pricing-table.js, which THIS PACKAGE NEVER EMITS. The demonstration project loads it in base.html's {% block provider_library %}, labelled a demonstration convenience — it is already there and this story does not change it.

DEMO VALUES — demo/settings.py already carries 'DRF_STRIPE_PRICING_TABLE_ID': 'prctbl_not_a_real_table' and 'DRF_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY': 'pk_test_not_a_real_key'. The landing page placement supplies its values as ATTRIBUTES, the way a project's own template would; how it reaches those two strings is yours to choose, but the point of the placement is that the component is given them directly rather than reading them itself.

COMPONENTS AVAILABLE — django-mvp 0.23.0 ships the Cotton components the demo's pages are assembled from, resolved under the project virtualenv's site-packages/mvp — read its templates/cotton/ directory rather than guessing at attributes. demo/templates/demo/home.html is built from <c-section>, <c-text>, <c-grid> and <c-card>; match the page's existing shape and copy voice rather than introducing a new idiom for one block.
spec_sections: User Story 3 - The same plans on a page of the project's own
prior_decisions: The component reads no settings and requires no view. That is the guarantee this story tests; do not add a context processor, a template tag or a view to make the landing-page placement work.

The component imposes no sign-in requirement of its own (FR-009). It must render for an anonymous visitor with no address and no error — US-2 already omits customer-email entirely in that case, which is correct and is not yours to change.
D4 — SC-002 is a guarantee about this package's output, not about the demonstration project's page. The demo loads the provider's library; that is expected and is not a violation to fix.

D2 — the script-absence guarantee is held at the template source. tests/test_app.py already asserts no shipped template under mvp_payments/ carries a script element with a host src; that is a pre-existing test and is not yours to touch.

WATCH — T016 may pass the moment it is written, because US-1 built the component to satisfy exactly this. Report which it was, honestly. A test that passes on first run here is evidence the design held.

WATCH — assert against rendered output, never against the presence of a class name (constitution Article XVI). For the query-count assertion use django_assert_num_queries(0) around a render carrying only the attributes.
WATCH — the demo landing page is a page a visitor reaches WITHOUT signing in. Do not place the component behind a login, and assert the anonymous case in tests/test_demo.py.

acceptance.given_when_then: Given the component rendered in a template unrelated to any page of this package, with a pricing table identifier and a publishable key as its only attributes, when it renders for an anonymous visitor, then the complete provider element is produced from those attributes alone (scenarios 1 and 2); and given that same render wrapped in django_assert_num_queries(0), then it completes without a single query, demonstrating it needs no view, no context processor and no backend (scenario 3).
Given an anonymous visitor opening the demonstration project's landing page, when it renders, then the provider's element is present on it with the demo's values.

Given the demonstration project's landing page, when a visitor who is not signed in opens it, then the pricing table appears there with a line of copy saying it is the same component the Account Center's Plans page renders.
